sentences.text: Dated this the 09th day of January, 2025 The 3rd respondent in OP (MV).No.747 of 2009 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Neyattinkara is the appellant herein.
The petitioners in the O.P.(MV) are the cross objectors.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)

2. The petitioners are the wife, children and parents of deceased by name Thomas, who died on 03.05.2008 in pursuance to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 30.04.2009.
The petitioners filed the O.P under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation.

According to the petitioners, while the deceased was standing on the side of the public road, a goods vehicle bearing Registration No.KL-01-AH-3287, driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, hit him down.

As a result of the accident, he sustained fatal injuries,
and he succumbed to the injuries while under treatment.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A12, Exts.B1 and B2.
MACA NO. 1606 OF 2017 & CO No.91 of 2017 2025:KER:1840 The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.13,86,700/- rounded to Rs.13,87,000/-.
Aggrieved by the award, the 3rd respondent preferred MACA No.1606 of 2017 and the petitioners preferred the cross objection.

4. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

5. Heard Sri.P.Jacob Mathew, the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the insurance company, and Sri.R.Nikhil, the learned Counsel for the cross objectors.
6.
The Point: In this case the accident and valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
Though in the written statement the 3 rd respondent has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased, at the time of arguments such a contention was not taken.
The petitioners produced Ext.A3, copy of the final report involved in the crime registered against the driver of the offending vehicle, in respect to the above accident.
In the light of the above charge sheet, negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle stands proved.
Therefore, the 3 rd respondent, being the insurer, is liable to indemnify the compensation, which is liable to be awarded against the owner of the offending vehicle.

The contention raised by the learned Senior Counsel who is appearing for the 3rd respondent is that the Tribunal has added 30% of the income towards future prospects, and it ought to have been 25% in the light of the dictum laid down in the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further he would argue that the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium and another Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of love and affection and Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expense which are on the higher side in the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra).

He would also argue that the notional income fixed by the Tribunal M.Sarojam vs Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69400/
3 is on the higher side.

sentences.text: 8. On the other hand, the learned for the cross objectors would argue that the notional income fixed by the Tribunal is correct.
9. At the time of the accident on 03.04.2009 the deceased was aged 46 years.
As per the claim petition, he was working as a Head load worker.
The petitioner claimed the monthly income of Rs.8,000/- and the same was accepted by the Tribunal on the basis of Ext.A12 - salary certificate.

The learned Senior Counsel would argue that as per the dictum laid down in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance [(2011) 13 SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie during the year 2009 would come to Rs.7,000/- only and hence, the notional income of the MACA NO. 1606 OF 2017 & CO No.91 of 2017 2025:KER:1840 deceased cannot be fixed above Rs.7,000/-.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However,
it appears that Ext.A12 - salary certificate was marked without objection, and as such I do not find merits to interfere with the notional income of Rs.8,000/- fixed by the Tribunal.

10. Since, on the date of accident, the deceased was aged 46 years, only 25% of his income could be added towards future prospects, in the light of the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 13.
11.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The deceased being married and having 5 dependants, deduction towards his personal and living expense is 1/4 of his income , in the light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

entities.text:
Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation [(2009) 6 SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.11,70,000/-
12.
As argued by the learned Senior Counsel, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards funeral expenses is on the higher side.

As per the dictum laid down in Pranay Sethi (supra), the petitioners are entitled to get only Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expense and Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three years.

Therefore, towards loss of estate, they are entitled MACA NO. 1606 OF 2017 & CO No.91 of 2017 2025:KER:1840 to get Rs.18,150/-, towards funeral expense Rs.18,150/- and towards loss of consortium Rs.48,400/- each.
13.

It appears that though in the Original Petition, the parents of the deceased were also parties as petitioners 4 and 5, during the pendency of the Original Petition itself, they died and the legal heirs were seen impleaded.
Even in the memorandum of appeal, the petitioners 1 to 3 alone are made appellants and the legal heirs of the deceased petitioners 4 and 5 were not impleaded.
In effect, 3 dependents of the deceased alone are there in the party array.
In the above circumstances, I hold that the petitioners 1 to 3 alone are entitled to get compensation towards loss of consortium at the rate of Rs.48,400/-.
Therefore, the compensation towards loss of consortium will come to Rs.1,45,200/- (48,400 x 3).

4 14.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards love and affection.

Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further amount for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v. Somwati and Others,
(2020)9 SCC 644.

entities.text:
New India Assurance Company Ltd. v. Somwati and Others,
(2020)9 SCC 644
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the above sum of Rs.1,00,000/- given towards love and affection is to be deducted.

15. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.20,000/-, which according to the learned counsel for the MACA NO. 1606 OF 2017 & CO No.91 of 2017 2025:KER:1840 petitioner, is on the lower side.

Though the accident was occurred on 30.04.2009,
the deceased succumbed to the injuries only on 03.05.2009.

In the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering is on the lower side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.35,000/-.
16.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

17. Therefore, the petitioner/ cross objector is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.14,31,600/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.

Head of claim

Amount awarded by The amount given the Tribunal(Rs) in appeal (Rs.) 1 Loss of dependency 1081600 11,70,000 2 Loss of consortium 100000 145200 3 Loss of estate 15000 18150 4 Funeral expenses 25000 18150 5 Loss of love and affection 100000 Nil 6 Loss of pain and sufferings 20000 35000 7
Medical expenses 39000 39000 MACA NO. 1606 OF 2017 & CO No.91 of 2017 2025:KER:1840 8 Transport to hospital 5000 5000
Total 13,86,700 14,31,600 rounded to 13,87,000 Amount enhanced 44,600

In the result, this Appeal and Cross Objection are disposed as follows :
The 3rd respondent is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs.14,31,600/-
(Rupees Fourteen Lakh Thirty One Thousand Six Hundred Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 9% per annum, from the date of the petition till realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

18. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioners, in the ratio fixed by the Tribunal, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay and as per rules.

Sd/-
